quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?

options.text: One driver should keep driving without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all vehicles must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
They will always get a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have what kind of blind spots?
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Big trucks and SUVs have areas behind them that cannot be seen in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: When can you turn left with the right-of-way?

options.text: At a green arrow pointing left.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a green arrow pointing left.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are not working?

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights do not work, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop and yield. Go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with speed and road conditions.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right?

options.text: When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane.
Even if you drive off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right when there is a passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow diamonds with black symbols. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you about a steep hill. Slow down to drive safely.

questions.question: What should you do at a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Go through if there is no crossing traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You can turn right at a red light if there is no sign saying you cannot.

questions.question: When you approach an accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your focus on your own driving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Focus on your own driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to an accident, fire, or disaster just to look.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Get into a routine when you enter and leave your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how quickly you can stop. Reduce your speed on poor roads to keep control of your car. Driving too fast on slippery roads puts you at risk if you need to stop suddenly.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment depends on:

options.text: Whether you drink beer instead of wine.
Whether you drink wine instead of beer.
Whether you drink hard ciders and mixed drinks.
How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: All types of alcohol harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed all the time.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers get distracted. A good defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. You must slow down as you approach the intersection and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right side of the road angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.

questions.explanation: A solid line at the road's edge marks the boundary between the driving lane and the shoulder. When the line angles toward the center of the road, it means the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: An arrow painted on the road means:

options.text: Drivers may choose to follow the direction of the arrow.
Drivers must follow the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers must always stop before following the arrow.
Drivers must follow the arrow while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must follow the arrow while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells drivers they must go in that direction. Follow all traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs mean:
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you of railroad crossings. Yield to trains and do not try to race across the tracks.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you finish the turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the center of the street.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When you turn left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These make roads slippery. When road conditions are poor, you may need to drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangle signs mean:
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangle signs tell drivers to yield. When it is safe and the road is clear, you may proceed.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic or within 500 feet of traffic ahead. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways on all tracks before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait for it to pass before you go.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go the same direction.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means drivers in both directions may pass. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: If you drive in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you can see less than 500 feet ahead. Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and reduce your visibility.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive the same way you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stay farther behind other vehicles. Your car needs more time to stop when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on your left, and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist when it is safe. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, then proceed only when safe.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or the arrow turns green.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or the arrow turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Do not move until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are in the wrong lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your signal and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Change lanes safely, then back up to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are in the wrong lane, drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires properly filled with air.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lane. A bicyclist is ahead going the same way. How should you pass safely?

options.text: Slow down, wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to warn the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space, or 5 feet on high-speed roads. Do not honk unless necessary, as it may startle the rider.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk.

questions.question: At night, how should you handle bright headlights from oncoming cars?

options.text: Look at the center of the road.
Look at the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look to the right side of the road ahead. Looking at the glare can temporarily blind you.
